role: @main entry of the watchOS app: holds the session manager and strap connector it takes from WatchDependencies.current, and a fresh workout manager, as @StateObjects, wires them together and builds the WatchLiveView scene.
types: WatchApp: struct (App, @main) — Watch app entry; its services come from the Watch composition root, WatchDependencies
toplevel: Stored-property initializers read WatchDependencies.current.sessionManager and .strapConnector (the process-wide instances unless a substitute is set) and construct a fresh WatchWorkoutManager. The file reads no `.shared` instance; WatchDependencies.swift is the Watch target's only root file in scripts/check_no_shared_outside_root.sh.

units.does: App init: reads WatchDependencies.current and attaches its session manager to its strap connector so direct-strap HR samples have a destination before any view exists. In the app these are WatchSessionManager.shared (first touch runs its init, activating WCSession) and WatchStrapConnector.shared.
units.entry: @main: SwiftUI instantiates WatchApp at process launch

units.does: Scene body: one WindowGroup showing WatchLiveView(sessionManager, workoutManager) with strapConnector injected as environment object; onAppear runs wireUp(), scenePhase changes go to followScenePhase, and displayOnlyMode changes (and the initial value) call strapConnector.setAutoReconnect(!displayOnly) so the wrist reconnects a saved strap only in legacy mode.

Scene phase change: .background → strapConnector.appDidEnterBackground() (ends any discovery scan); .active → sessionManager.requestCurrentStateFromPhone() (deduplicated with launch's in-flight pull).

branches.effect: false: return; true: pull current state

units.does: First-appear wiring: attaches the workout manager to the session manager (starting the keep-alive session if already recording), makes the workout manager follow phone messages (silence detection), requests HealthKit authorization in a Task, and pulls the current state from the iPhone.
